Mains are a choice of two steaks, such as strip loin and filet, or the signature sirloin with a crisp crust, eaten with rice and miso soup. tokyo_yakiuo_ishikawa_mitsukoshi.notes: [Seafood · fish grilled like yakiniku] A 24-seat restaurant on the 12th floor of the Ginza Mitsukoshi annex (13 at the counter, 9 in a private counter room), opened in 2025. It serves 'yaki-uo', a fish version of yakiniku developed over eight years by the founder of Tsukiji Aozora. Premium cuts are grilled in front of you, such as fatty tuna billed as 'special kalbi', with house condiments and sauces. 2026 diners started with the brain, then had fresh mehikari, a yukhoe-like dish and a sukiyaki-style course (just under ¥4,000 plus ¥400 service). The ladies' lunch adds rice with refills, cold noodles and dessert. The grill staff are chatty. Many guests are visitors from Hong Kong and Singapore. A touch salty, and slow at times.

tokyo_arbre_village_kimuraya_ginza4.notes: [French · above Ginza Kimuraya's bakery] A calm, well-spaced 32-seat French restaurant on the fourth floor of the Ginza Kimuraya building, formerly Restaurant Kimuraya. Big windows look down on Chūō-dōri. The chef once led the kitchen at the now-closed Maxim's de Paris in Ginza. The course runs appetizer, fish, meat and dessert, with two baskets of about four breads from the Kimuraya bakery below (famous for anpan, but the baguettes shine too). Takeaway bags are given for leftover bread, which used to be unlimited. Reservations are required. To reach the lift you walk through the busy shop, so try the second-floor entrance. About ¥6,000–8,000 at lunch.

tokyo_ginza_brio_ginza7.notes: [Yōshoku · French-leaning, on Hanatsubaki-dōri] A calm 31-seat seventh-floor restaurant open since 2021, with a counter, tables and a fully private room for six. A French chef cooks nostalgic yet fresh Western dishes to match wine and whisky. The highlight in April 2026 was a charcoal-grilled Hitachi-beef tenderloin, and lighter Italian-leaning plates suit a second stop. Courses or à la carte; plating is beautiful, portions on the small side, and one diner wanted more explanation of the dishes. Staff are friendly. About ¥5,000–15,000.

tokyo_hitsumabushi_bincho_mitsukoshi.notes: [Unagi · Nagoya's Bincho on the Mitsukoshi restaurant floor] The Ginza branch (its second in Tokyo) of Nagoya's long-established Bincho, on the 11th floor of Ginza Mitsukoshi. Eel is grilled directly without steaming, Kansai style: crisp outside, fluffy within. Eat the hitsumabushi as is, then with condiments, then with broth. Portions are generous; a ¾-eel size exists, and the rolled omelette is a good side. The nine-dish Bincho Kaiseki Takumi course (¥10,950) adds crab-miso tofu, bone senbei and grilled liver. Queues form, so book or come early. Many overseas visitors.

tokyo_haretari_kumottari_ginza_nine.notes: [Izakaya · Shōwa-retro seafood under the expressway] A 33-seat seafood izakaya in the basement of Ginza Nine 2, with a retro Shōwa feel and a family-like welcome that keeps regulars coming. Seafood is the strength: sashimi that wins over non-sashimi people, simmered, fried and grilled dishes. In October 2026 orders included a ¥2,300 grilled-fish set of thick, crisp-skinned mackerel, fried aori squid with sudachi (¥1,600) and salted yam fries (¥1,400). The weekday lunch includes menchi katsu and crab cream croquette sets with careful miso soup and sides, plus curry and kara-age; some items sell out early.

tokyo_orca_ginza_brewery.notes: [Craft beer · a microbrewery under Ginza 8-chōme] A 33-seat brewery restaurant (formerly Brew In Bar & Nature) in the basement space of a bar founded in 1985. Small stainless tanks brew about ten house beers, and staff show guests the brewhouse. The three-beer tasting is ¥2,200, with small fries at ¥900. Food runs to New Zealand grass-fed beef (one diner found it sinewy; the Wagyu had sold out) and many appetizers. Mostly overseas visitors, relaxed and unhurried. Opens mid-afternoon at weekends.
